title: BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting Opens in New Delhi — Iran-UAE Confrontation Dominates Day 1
detail: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar opened the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting at Bharat Mandapam convention center, New Delhi on May 14, 2026 — the highest-level multilateral event of India's 2026 BRICS chairmanship. Attendees included Russia's Sergey Lavrov (in person), Brazil's Mauro Vieira, South Africa's Ronald Lamola, Iran's Abbas Araghchi, Indonesia's Sugiono, and China's Ambassador Xu Feihong (FM Wang Yi was absent for US-China summit talks in Beijing). Prime Minister Modi met bilaterally with Foreign Ministers Lavrov and Araghchi on the sidelines — the first in-person India-Iran high-level contact since the Iran-related conflict escalated in early 2026. Day 1 discussions covered UN Security Council reform, BRICS payment infrastructure, the humanitarian situation in Gaza, Sudan, and Syria's political transition. Jaishankar called unilateral sanctions 'unjustifiable' in his national statement and advocated for safe maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. However, Iran FM Araghchi publicly accused the UAE of being 'directly involved in military actions against Iran,' prompting UAE FM Al Marar to issue a sharp rebuttal — a direct confrontation between two BRICS members that immediately overshadowed the meeting's multilateral agenda and blocked early consensus on joint language.

title: NDB 11th Annual Meeting Opens in Moscow — Technology, Nuclear Energy, and AI in Finance on Agenda
detail: The New Development Bank (NDB) convened its 11th Annual Meeting of the Board of Governors in Moscow, Russia on May 14-15, 2026 — the first NDB annual meeting held in Moscow and a decision taken at the 10th Annual Meeting in Rio de Janeiro during Brazil's 2025 chairmanship. The theme was 'Development Financing in an Era of Technological Revolution.' The pre-meeting seminar on May 13 addressed NDB support for nuclear power and nuclear medicine. The flagship Governors Seminar on May 14 covered financing development in the technological age, with satellite sessions on AI in finance, healthcare trends to 2030, universities of the new economy, and virtual assets. Speakers included Russian Deputy PM Alexey Overchuk, Deputy Finance Minister Ivan Chebeskov, and Columbia University's Jeffrey Sachs. The May 15 business session addressed ongoing NDB operations; the BRICS FM meeting in New Delhi simultaneously adopted language supporting 'further NDB membership expansion.' Russia's lending suspension (since Dec 2022) was not publicly resolved at the meeting. The NDB has approved $35.7 billion+ across 100+ projects globally, targeting 30% local currency lending by year-end 2026.

title: Modi Meets Iran FM Araghchi on BRICS Sidelines — First India-Iran High-Level Contact Since Iran War
detail: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a bilateral meeting with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi on May 14, 2026 — the first in-person high-level contact between India and Iran since the Iran-related conflict began in early 2026. The meeting covered regional security, bilateral trade relations (India is a major purchaser of Iranian oil, settled in rupees outside SWIFT), and India's offer to facilitate diplomatic engagement. Modi conveyed India's support for dialogue and diplomacy as the primary route to conflict resolution. The meeting is significant given India's position as a non-Western actor with active ties to both sides of regional tensions. External Affairs Minister Jaishankar separately held a formal bilateral with Araghchi on the conference sidelines. India's engagement reinforces its stated 'strategic autonomy' doctrine and the 'Humanity First' theme of its 2026 BRICS chairmanship.
